chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub and Ibn Bakeyr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who slanders another man, so he is whipped, and he repeats the slander against him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he says to him, "That which I said to you was true," he would not be whipped; and if he were to slander him with adultery after having been whipped, so upon him would be the Penalty (Hadd); and if he slanders him before he is whipped, by ten slanders, there would not happen to be upon him, except for one Penalty (Hadd).'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if a slanderer repeats his accusation after being whipped?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural nuances of *hadd al-qadhf* (flogging for slander), specifically addressing the legal status of a slanderer who retracts or reiterates his claim post-punishment. It establishes that a simple denial of truth exempts one from further lashes, whereas a fresh accusation of adultery incurs the penalty anew, while multiple prior accusations consolidated before the initial whipping result in a single hadd. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the timing of the accusation relative to the execution of punishment to determine liability.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub and Ibn Bakeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding the man who slanders the man, so he is whipped, and he repeats the slander against him. Heasws said: ‘If he says to him, ‘That which I said to you was true’, he would not be whipped; and if he were to slander with the adultery after having been whipped, so upon him would be the Penalty (Hadd); and if he slanders him before he is whipped, by ten slanders, there would not happen to be upon him, except for one Penalty (Hadd)’.
